transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess what brings me in is I’ve been getting a little stuck on how my face looks lately. Mostly around my jaw, like it seems kind of sagging or uneven on one side. It really stood out to me after seeing myself in some family photos.

I know that probably sounds minor, and my wife—and even clients—say they barely notice anything, so maybe I’m making too much of it. But it’s been on my mind enough that I thought I should ask someone about it, if that makes sense.
How often do you find yourself thinking about the appearance of your jaw or face, and does it interfere with your daily life?

I mean, I wouldn’t say it stops me from doing things completely. I’m still working, still seeing clients and everything. But… I do think about it more than I’d like to admit.

It can slow me down getting ready, especially before client meetings. I’ll check how my jaw looks and then feel like I need to adjust my shirt or angle my face or… I don’t know, just make sure it’s not obvious. And during some appointments I catch myself not being as present because part of my mind is on how I look.

I’ve also skipped a few art openings, which sounds kind of silly saying out loud, but I just didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. It’s not ruining my life or anything, but it is getting in the way some. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you noticed that your concern about your jaw is part of a bigger pattern of feeling down, anxious, or self-conscious, or does it mostly come up when you're specifically thinking about or seeing your face?

I think it mostly comes up when I’m looking at my face or I’m reminded of it—like in photos or before I’m seeing clients. It’s this sagging, uneven look around my jaw, especially one side, that I get stuck on.

I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, because my wife says she barely notices it and clients haven’t really reacted or anything. But once I see it, it’s hard for me to just let it go. Does that answer what you mean?
When you're focused on how your jaw looks, does it tend to leave you feeling hopeless, guilty, or like you’ve lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not sure I’d put it as hopeless or guilty, exactly. It’s more like I get embarrassed and a little frustrated with myself for caring about it so much.

I don’t think I’ve lost interest in things overall… at least not in a broad way. It’s more that if I’m already feeling self-conscious about my face, I might not feel like going to something where I’ll be seen. But I still enjoy my work and family and things like that. I hope that makes sense.
Do you ever have repeated, intrusive thoughts about your jaw that you try not to have, but they keep coming back despite your efforts?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it does keep coming back.

What brings me in is that I keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. Especially after I saw myself in all those family photos, it was like I couldn’t unsee it. I’ll try to tell myself my wife says she barely notices, and clients don’t seem to notice anything either, but the thought still pops back in.

It’s not like I’m trying to think about it, if that makes sense. I’d rather not be focused on it. But once it’s in my head, it’s hard to just move on.

When these thoughts about your jaw come up, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking your face, adjusting how you look, or going over it in your mind—to try to feel better or make the thoughts go away?

Yeah… I do, though I feel a little embarrassed saying it because it sounds vain.

Before client meetings, I’ll usually check the bathroom mirror, and sometimes my phone camera too, more than once. I’ll adjust the lighting or turn my face a certain way, maybe fix my collar, just to see if it makes my jaw look less uneven.

And then later, if I’m around other people—like younger advisors or at gallery events—I catch myself comparing my face to theirs instead of really staying focused on the conversation. It’s not constant, but it happens enough that I notice it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself similarly concerned about other parts of your body, or is your main focus specifically on your jaw and face?

It’s mostly my jaw and face, I’d say. I don’t really get caught up in other body parts the same way.

What brings me in is more that I keep noticing this sagging, kind of uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. It got a lot worse in my mind after seeing myself in those family photos, like I couldn’t quite stop seeing it after that.

I know my wife says she barely notices, and clients don’t seem to notice anything, so maybe I’m making too much of it… but that’s the area I keep coming back to.
When you think about how your jaw looks, does it feel like a minor annoyance or does it cause you significant distress, like feeling unattractive or flawed in a way that really bothers you?

It’s… more than a minor annoyance, I think. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I know my wife says she barely notices and clients don’t seem to notice anything, but it really does bother me.

I keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. After I saw those family photos, it was like it became harder to ignore. I feel unattractive when I notice it, or like there’s something off about my face, even if part of me knows other people may not see it the same way. Does that make sense?
